yak.types: Yak fiber comes in two main forms: fine down, the insulating undercoat collected at the molt and dehaired for textiles, and coarse outer hair traditionally used for ropes, tents and rugs. Reported down diameters are roughly 16 to 20 microns, overlapping the coarser end of cashmere, with average down length of about 3.5 to 5 cm in one study of grey and black yaks. Hand dehairing tends to leave more coarse hair and raise the average diameter. Color is the other key variable: most yak fiber is brown, grey or black, while white down from breeds such as the Tianzhu White Yak is scarce. Trade forms include dehaired down, tops, yarn and blends, especially yak with merino.
yak.fabrics: Dehaired yak down is spun into knitting yarn and made into sweaters, scarves, hats and socks, often in natural brown or grey. Blends with merino wool add elasticity and length for base layers and outdoor knitwear, and blends with silk add luster to scarves. Woven yak and wool cloth is used for throws, blankets and some coatings. Coarse yak hair appears in felted and woven rugs, bags and traditional tent cloth on the plateau. Undyed yarns are common because bleaching to pale shades costs fiber strength.
yak.quality: Ask for 'yak down' rather than 'yak hair' or 'yak wool', since the terms can hide a coarse fraction. Good yak down feels soft and dry with a matte surface; visible straight, dark, stiff fibers indicate poor dehairing and will prickle. Very pale yak products have been bleached, which can weaken fiber and harshen hand. Check blend percentages: 'yak blend' may be mainly wool. Because yak down is a documented adulterant in cashmere, a product labeled cashmere should not contain it, and a cheap 'cashmere' in natural brown deserves questions. In the US, yak must be named with the word hair or fiber, not called wool or cashmere.
pros: Fine down gives soft, warm knits comparable in hand to coarser cashmere.
Natural browns and greys allow undyed products.
Down is gathered at the molt from herds kept mainly for milk, meat and transport, so fiber is a co-product.
Merino blends combine yak's softness with wool's spring.
cons: Short down fibers pill and wear in lightly twisted yarns.
Residual guard hair causes prickle and dark specks.
Pale colors require bleaching that weakens the fiber.
Labeling is confusing, and yak is a common undeclared adulterant in cashmere.
yak.impact: Yak down is a co-product of plateau herding, so its footprint is tied to how pastures are grazed rather than to fiber-specific inputs. A 2017 study of family yak farms on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau measured greenhouse gases from meadows, dung, manure heaps and night pens and found that methane and nitrous oxide made up about 21% and 45% of annual global warming potential, so gases other than carbon dioxide cannot be ignored. Grazing intensity matters: in a 2024 yak grazing experiment on the eastern plateau, heavier grazing reduced ecosystem multifunctionality and carbon and nitrogen cycling. No peer-reviewed life cycle assessment per kilogram of yak down was found. Herder income from down depends on collection and dehairing, and bleaching pale yak adds chemical inputs.
yak.care: Follow the label. Hand wash in cool water (about 30 C or below) with a wool detergent free of enzymes and bleach, or use a wool cycle only if permitted. Avoid rubbing and wringing; press water out, roll in a towel and dry flat. Never tumble dry. Steam or press at the two-dot setting (up to 150 C) through a cloth if needed. Remove pills with a comb or shaver once early pilling settles. Fold for storage, keep pieces clean, and protect them from moth and carpet beetle larvae with sealed storage and regular checks.
faq: Is yak wool as soft as cashmere?

Fine yak down, reported at roughly 16 to 20 microns, overlaps the coarser end of cashmere, so well-dehaired yak can feel similar. Softness depends on how thoroughly coarse hair was removed and on yarn and knit construction, so compare actual garments rather than fiber names.
Why is most yak yarn brown?

Most yaks have dark, melanin-rich coats, so the down is naturally brown, grey or black. White yak is scarce, and pale shades usually require bleaching, which can weaken the fiber and roughen its surface. Many makers therefore sell yak undyed or overdyed in dark colors.
How is yak labeled in the US?

Yak is not one of the specialty fibers named in the US wool law, so it is disclosed under the textile rules as yak hair or yak fiber when it makes up 5% or more, or under the general term fur fiber. It must never be called cashmere.
notable: On family yak farms studied on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, methane and nitrous oxide together made up about two-thirds of annual global warming potential.
Hand-dehaired yak down measured coarser on average than machine-dehaired down in one fiber study, because more guard hair remained.
